text:
# Plane Composing Algorithms

Also called: Image Order Volume Rendering, Slicing Method

## Overview
Plane Composing Algorithms are [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) methods that operate by [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) several slices which comprise a volumetric model [S1, S2, S3, unofficial]. They tend to work best when the view-plane is fixed parallel to the model, so that each of the voxels being composed may be accessed on separate planes [S1, S2, unofficial]. This approach is distinct from [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) [Ray Casting](42-ray-casting.md) in that it processes data in object-order slices rather than image-order rays, and it differs from [Texture Slicing](845-texture-slicing.md) by explicitly defining the composition logic of those slices rather than relying solely on hardware texture interpolation.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves dividing the volume into slices (planes) and composing them one over the other to produce the final image [S3, unofficial]. The computational complexity is relative to the volume size [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

**Composition Order:**
Planes can be composed from rear to front or front to back [S3, unofficial].
*   **Rear to Front:** If composed rear to front, the accumulation of color and transparency uses specific equations starting with initial values (typically zero color and zero opacity) [S3, unofficial].
*   **Front to Back:** If composed front to back, the [standard ray casting](#12643-standard-ray-casting.md) accumulation equations remain valid [S3, unofficial].

**[Geometric Constraints](#9270-geometry-and-surface-priors.md):**
The method works best when the view-plane is parallel to the volume edge [S3, unofficial]. In this case, voxels can be accessed easily as planes in the volume [S3, unofficial]. If the view-plane is not parallel to the volume, a more complicated sampling algorithm is needed [S3, unofficial].

**Filtering:**
Since a voxel is not projected onto one pixel, a filter should be used for the composition to handle aliasing and interpolation [S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### Slice Plane Ordering
See [Slice Plane Ordering](4041-slice-plane-ordering.md) for details on the specific ordering strategies used to traverse the planes during composition.

### Transparent Planes
**Definition:** A strategy that slices the volume by many planes, applies a transfer function to each vertex on the plane to create variation in color and transparency, and renders the planes from back to front [S4, unofficial].

**Parameters:** The number of planes is typically between 200 and 1000 [S4, unofficial].

**Comparison:** These planes can be quickly rendered using 2D textures or 3D textures [S4, unofficial].

## Background
Plane Composing Algorithms are one of the two main categories of direct volume rendering algorithms, the other being Ray Casting [S1, S2, unofficial]. They were identified as a primary technique for rendering volumes based on their ability to exploit spatial coherency and texture-based rendering hardware [S1, S2, unofficial].

Performance improvements for this method include [Shear-Warp factorization of the viewing matrix](#787-shear-warp-algorithm.md), which applies a shearing transformation to exploit spatial coherency of the model, reducing computational complexity of rendering a volume from an arbitrary viewing angle [S1, S2, unofficial]. Other optimizations mentioned include using information of min-max non-transparent voxels, interleaving methods (such as sampling only half of the planes or ¼ of the points in the image), and using hardware graphic accelerators to send volume planes one by one as transparent textures [S3, unofficial].
